subject: Harmonic-tenor renewal proposal + canary onramp (2yr)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: Harmonic-tenor renewal proposal + canary onramp (2yr)

Hi Eliza —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Per our follow-up, attached is a concise proposal that attempts to balance NovaFabric's need for predictable unit economics with the flexibility to scale quickly during product launches. High level:

- Term structure: 24 months (harmonic-tenor to co-term with your FYQ1 end) with a staged ramp schedule rather than a flat commit.
- Staged ramp (tokens/month, illustrative): months 1–3 baseline (100k), months 4–9 progressive ramp to 350k, months 10–24 steady-state (350k+ with monthly burst allowance).
- Canary onramp: 30-day canary window for new model/quantization profile with a 20% reserved burst and two KPI gates (latency 95th < 220ms, quality regressions < 1.2% over eval set). Canary is opt-in for the first rollout and automatically scales if KPIs are met.
- Auto-renew: proposed 60-day opt-out notice prior to renewal; open to discussion on the notice window.
- Pricing: blended rate for year 1 (onramp-discount) then step to steady-state unit pricing in year 2; proposed credits for early payment and a one-time onboarding credit to offset migration costs.
- Co-terming: we will align your account term to FYQ1 with pro-rata for the initial period so future renewals match your fiscal cadence.

Attachments: RD-2026-NovaFabric-proposal.pdf (proposal), NovaFabric_SOW_draft.docx (SOW + milestones).

Questions for you:
1) Is the 30-day canary window acceptable or would you prefer a longer staged pilot?
2) Do you have constraints on auto-renew notice period from procurement/legal?
3) Preferred billing cadence: monthly or quarterly invoicing?

If helpful I can carve out 30 minutes with Karthik (pricing) and Grace (onboarding/CS) to walk through the timeline and the canary checklist.

Thanks — look forward to your feedback.

—
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Harmonic-tenor renewal proposal + canary onramp (2yr)

Hi Soojin —

Appreciate the detailed deck and SOW. A few quick notes from procurement and engineering:

- Procurement is mandated to keep auto-renew windows to a maximum of 30 days (we push back on longer notice periods for multi-year deals). Can procurement share the contractual language that requires 60 days?
- For billing cadence: we typically do monthly consumption invoicing but prefer quarterly committed-invoice for budget planning. Can you show both examples?
- Engineering flagged the 30-day canary as potentially tight for our security/regression testing during launch weeks — they'd prefer a 45–60 day pilot.
- Also, please share SOC 2 Type II evidence and a brief on data retention controls for the private deployment option (we may require the private control plane for PII-sensitive workloads).

We are generally comfortable with a two-year engagement if the canary and billing cadence can be aligned. Can you loop in legal on the auto-renew language and provide an updated pricing schedule reflecting monthly vs quarterly billing?

Thanks — I copied procurement so they can weigh in on the contractual notice.

Best,
Eliza
Eliza Monroe
Head of Platform Engineering | NovaFabric
eliza.monroe@novafabric.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Harmonic-tenor renewal proposal + canary onramp (2yr)

Soojin —

Saw Eliza's asks. Proposed changes we should offer to keep the deal moving while protecting Redwood's economics:

1) Auto-renew: shift to a 90-day opt-out window in contract language unless NovaFabric is willing to accept a 30-day window in exchange for a modest price premium. We can present both options: (A) 60-day (our original) / (B) 90-day with better price/credit / (C) 30-day with +4% surcharge.

2) Canary: increase pilot to 45 days (compromise) and include a two-stage KPI gate: after day 21 (initial pass) and day 45 (full green). Offer an engineering-runbook and rollback playbook (hosted fallback) as part of onboarding. The 30% reserved burst for launch weeks is also acceptable.

3) Billing cadence: offer both monthly consumption invoices and an optional quarterly committed invoice that smooths budget forecasting. For quarterly commit we propose a 1.5% discount on invoice amounts.

4) SOC 2 / private deployment: provide SOC 2 Type II report redacted + private control plane checklist. Ask security to prepare a 1-page summary for Eliza.

5) DocuSign & SOW: I'll prepare two contract exhibits (pricing schedule A & B) so legal can toggle the auto-renew clause. Please add the HubSpot deal id and send the DocuSign once Eliza signals which auto-renew option she prefers.

I also recommend highlighting an early-payment onboarding credit (1 month free) to reduce friction.

If you want, I can be on the next call to negotiate the auto-renew tradeoffs.

- Karthik

- Canary window: updated to 45 days with a two-stage KPI gate (day 21 quick pass; day 45 full validation). Engineering-runbook + rollback plan included in SOW exhibit.
- Auto-renew: we can present three options in contract exhibit A: 30-day opt-out (+4% surcharge), 60-day opt-out (baseline), 90-day opt-out (baseline price + onboarding credit). Legal language is in the attached pricing exhibits.
- Billing cadence: provided example schedules for monthly consumption invoicing and quarterly committed invoicing (quarterly = 1.5% discount).
- SOC 2 / Private deployment: attached redacted SOC 2 Type II statement and a 1-page private-control-plane checklist.

Answers to your questions:

2) Auto-renew contractual language — included as three toggles in Exhibit B. Procurement can pick the preferred clause; DocuSign link below will point to the selected exhibit.
3) Billing examples — both monthly and quarterly options are in page 6 of the proposal.

Next steps:

- If procurement prefers the quarterly committed invoice, confirm target invoice dates and we will mirror them in the SOW milestones.
- Tentative canary kickoff: the week of Oct 4 (if timeline works for your release schedule).
